title: Mobility Equipment Manufacturer Warranty Terms — Early-Failure Teardown and Gearbox Alignment on Drive Units
content:
# Early-Failure Teardown and Gearbox Alignment — Mobility Equipment Drive Units

**Term.** On a warranty drive motor or gearbox replacement of a Mobility Equipment chair, the drive-unit allowance claimed from the manufacturer is set by the days from the chair's delivery date to the day the drive-unit claim is posted:

1. **No more than 14 days** — the manufacturer's early-failure teardown of the whole drive train applies and the allowance is the standard drive-unit allowance doubled.
2. **More than 14 but no more than 90 days** — the allowance is the standard drive-unit allowance plus 2 units for aligning the opposite gearbox.
3. **A longer span** — the standard drive-unit allowance applies unchanged.

## Schedule

| Days from the delivery date to the posting day | Drive-unit allowance |
|---|---|
| 0 to 14 | the standard drive-unit allowance doubled (early-failure teardown) |
| 15 to 90 | the standard drive-unit allowance plus 2 units (opposite gearbox alignment) |
| 91 or more | the standard drive-unit allowance, unchanged |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, chair delivered 10 February of a non-leap year)

- Claim posted 24 February: 14 days — doubled.
- Claim posted 25 February: 15 days — plus 2 units.
- Claim posted 11 May: 90 days — plus 2 units.
- Claim posted 12 May: 91 days — unchanged.
